keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aussie pub-rock meets Caribbean reggae skank in E major, punctuated by gritty blues-rock soloing
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C# minor is the relative minor of E major

mainProgression.description: Bouncy reggae-influenced upbeat stabs during the verse that explode into an irresistible Australian pub-rock singalong chorus.

sectionProgressions.description: Staccato upbeat reggae chops on beats 2 and 4 with tight fret-hand dampening

sectionProgressions.progression: A - B - E - C#m - A - B - E
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: IV - V - I - vi - IV - V - I
sectionProgressions.description: Immortal pub anthem hook ('Cheap wine and a three day growth') shifting from subdominant IV straight to dominant V
Minor introspective breakdown building tension ahead of the guitar solo

harmonicFunction: E (I) - Warm major tonic providing stability and relaxed coastal groove
A (IV) - Subdominant chord initiating the uplifting chorus ascent
B (V) - Driving dominant engine providing relentless forward resolution
C#m (vi) - Relative minor adding bitter-sweet emotional depth to the chorus turnaround
G#m (iii) - Mediant minor chord creating a classic stepping-stone in the bridge

techniques.name: Staccato Reggae Skank & Upbeat Chops
techniques.description: Crisp upbeat chord stabs on beats 2 and 4 using quick fret-hand release for percussive chop dynamics

sequence: Strike the top 3-4 strings cleanly on the upbeat (& of 1, & of 2, etc.)
Instantly release finger pressure to choke the chord sustain
Transition into driving downstrokes when Jimmy Barnes enters on the chorus
tips: Use a Fender Stratocaster in the middle or neck/middle pickup position for authentic hollow quack
Keep the right wrist relaxed and bouncing continuously in 16th notes
Add slight palm muting to the bass strings between chops

techniques.name: Ian Moss Blues-Rock Phrasing & Sweet Major Thirds
techniques.description: Blending fiery E minor blues aggression with sweet E major 3rd chord tones (G#), crying vocal vibrato, and soaring whole-step bends

notes: Target sweet E major 3rd (G#) at 13th fret on string 3
Execute full whole-step bends from 14th fret F# up to G# on string 3, and 15th fret D up to E on string 2
Apply wide, singing finger vibrato on sustained notes
sequence: Establish high-register presence with a singing 12th-to-15th fret line over E major
Resolve smoothly to the G# sweet note as the chord shifts
Dig in with pick dynamics for Ian Moss's trademark vocal bite
tips: Use your thumb over the neck for leverage when pushing whole-step bends
Slightly roll off the guitar tone knob to 7 for Ian Moss's warm, singing woman tone
Add an overdrive pedal (Tube Screamer) to push tube amps into fluid singing compression

sections.name: Intro Wurlitzer & Reggae Upbeat Chops
sections.description: Don Walker's mellow Wurlitzer electric piano establishes the Caribbean bounce, joined by Ian Moss's crisp staccato upbeat chops.
notes: Wait for the Wurlitzer intro before entering on the upbeat of beat 2
Choke the high E and B strings with the underside of your fretting fingers
Keep the rhythm strictly locked to the 118 BPM pocket

sections.name: Verse 1 Reggae Skank Groove
sections.description: Ian Moss's light-fingered reggae groove accompanying Don Walker's Wurlitzer piano and Steve Prestwich's snare rim click.
notes: Choke the strings immediately after striking on beats 2 and 4
Focus on the treble triad on strings 1, 2, and 3
Leave dynamic space for Jimmy Barnes's gritty storytelling verse vocal

sections.name: Chorus 1 Pub-Rock Power Hook
sections.description: Full band explosion into the legendary 'Cheap wine and a three day growth' chorus, shifting from staccato chops to wide resonant downstrokes.
sections.progression: A - B - E - C#m - A - B - E
notes: Switch from staccato skanks to wide, resonant power strums across all strings
Hit the A to B push with aggressive downstroke attack
Slide cleanly into the C#m barre chord at fret 4 to emphasize the emotional lift

sections.name: Bridge Minor Walkdown
sections.description: An atmospheric minor breakdown ('Sitting on the sofa, listening to the rain') creating emotional tension before the guitar solo.
notes: Ease back on pick velocity for a reflective, moody dynamic
Let the 4th-fret C#m and G#m barre chords resonate with warm sustain
Crescendo across the B major barre chord to launch Ian Moss's guitar solo

sections.name: Ian Moss's Iconic Blues-Rock Guitar Solo
sections.description: One of the crowning guitar solos of Australian rock history. Ian Moss combines screaming E minor pentatonic bends with sweet E major 3rds (G# at 13th fret), weeping vibrato, and lightning descending blues runs.
sections.progression: E - A - B - E - C#m - A - B
notes: Start on the high E and B strings at the 12th fret with lyrical, vocal-like phrasing
Hit the 13th fret G string (G#) to outline the E major tonic triad sweetly
Unleash a wide whole-step bend on the 15th fret B string with sustained vibrato
Cascade down the E minor blues box (15-12 on B, 14-12 on G, 14 on D) into the 12th-fret double-stop resolution

sections.name: Final Outro Chorus & Climax
sections.description: Jimmy Barnes delivers maximum vocal intensity while Ian Moss peppers the driving pub rock rhythm with high-register blues fills as the song fades out.
sections.progression: A - B - E - C#m (repeating to fade)
notes: Drive the chorus rhythm with confident, full downstrokes
Sprinkle 12th and 15th fret blues bends between vocal lines
Lock tight with Prestwich's crashing ride cymbal through the outro fade

guitar.pickup: Middle pickup or neck/middle in-between quack position

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50W or Fender Twin Reverb

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS808 Tube Screamer for transparent mid-hump solo boost
effects.reverb: Spring reverb set to moderate wash
effects.other: MXR Phase 90 or subtle analog chorus for verse movement

beginner.title: Mastering the Open Chords
steps: Learn open E, A, and B7 (or B barre) chord changes cleanly
Practice steady quarter-note strums along with the chorus
Memorize the IV - V - I - vi chorus sequence
beginner.goals: Seamless transitions between E, A, B, and C#m

intermediate.title: Reggae Skank Dynamics & Upbeat Timing
steps: Practice fret-hand muting on the offbeats of beats 2 and 4
Coordinate with a metronome at 118 BPM using the 8th-note subdivision
Play full verse-to-chorus dynamic transitions without dropping beats
intermediate.goals: Tight, authentic funk-reggae pocket on the verses

advanced.title: Ian Moss Lead Fills & Soloing
steps: Transcribe Ian Moss's soaring blues-rock solo in E minor pentatonic
Master the expressive whole-step bends at the 12th and 14th frets
Blend major 3rd (G#) sweet notes with minor 3rd (G) blues bends
advanced.goals: Full lead guitar mastery with vocal-like phrasing and sustain

commonMistakes: Letting the verse upbeat chords ring out too long instead of choking them immediately
Rushing the tempo during the transition from the quiet bridge into the final chorus
Over-bending the G note on string 2 (15th fret) during the solo fills
practiceRoutine: Practice 5 minutes of fret-hand muting with a metronome set to 118 BPM
Loop the chorus progression (A - B - E - C#m) focusing on smooth barre chord shifts
Jam over the E major backing track with E minor blues scale double-stops
focusAreas: Percussive fret-hand relaxation for clean reggae skank
Dynamic contrast between low-volume verse and roaring chorus
Expressive finger vibrato on sustained lead notes
metronomeWork: Set click to 90 BPM to nail the upbeat skank pocket cleanly
Ramp up to 118 BPM using the Speed Trainer tool in +3 BPM steps
Practice with clicks only on beats 2 and 4 to build authentic reggae feel
